title: Time step too large — PISO pressure-velocity coupling diverged
symptoms: Courant number climbed steadily past 1 and reached 6 by t=0.05; continuity errors grew every outer iteration; solver aborted with FOAM FATAL ERROR after 'Continuity errors cannot be removed'. Residuals for p rose instead of falling. deltaT was fixed at 0.001 with no adjustTimeStep.
root_cause: Fixed deltaT far above the mesh Courant limit: the explicit correction terms in the PISO loop blow up once Courant exceeds ~1, so continuity can no longer be removed and pressure diverges.
fix: Enable adjustTimeStep with maxCo=0.5 (and maxDeltaT as a ceiling), restart from the last stable time directory, and re-check the Courant number in the first 50 steps. If the run must keep a fixed deltaT, coarsen the mesh near small cells instead.

title: Mesh non-orthogonality too high — gradient blow-up
symptoms: checkMesh reported Max aspect ratio 41 and Max concaveness 0.87; 912 faces above 70 degrees non-orthogonality. Solver ran a few hundred iterations with slowly growing p residuals, then died with 'Floating point exception' in the gradient scheme. gaussGrad was used with no limiter.
root_cause: Highly non-orthogonal cells (snappyHexMesh layer collapse near curved walls) make the default Gaussian gradient correction unstable; the correction term grows with non-orthogonality and eventually overflows.
fix: Switch gradSchemes to leastSquares or add a limited form (e.g. 'gauss linear 0.5' style limiter / cellLimited), regenerate the boundary layers with more relaxation iterations, and locally refine where non-orthogonality exceeds 65 degrees. Re-run checkMesh until faces >70 degrees are below ~0.1%.

title: Outlet boundary condition backflow — reversed flow at patch
symptoms: Log showed 'Reversed flow (outlet) detected on 3400 of 12000 faces' from the first iteration; U residuals plateaued at 1e-2 and never dropped; solution drifted until a bounded variable (k) went negative and crashed the run with 'Floating point exception'.
root_cause: A fixedValue outlet velocity BC forced inflow where the recirculation zone actually exits the domain backward, injecting unphysical momentum and eventually driving k negative.
fix: Change the outlet to pressure-driven (fixedValue p + inletOutlet U), or move the outlet patch further downstream past the recirculation; use inletOutlet with a safe inflowValue for k/epsilon so any backflow enters with physical turbulence values.

title: Turbulence initialization too aggressive — k spiked on step 1
symptoms: First iteration already reported 'bounding k, min: -240' and 'bounding epsilon, min: -18'; nut shot up to 40x the laminar value; the effective viscosity destroyed the boundary layer and the momentum equation diverged within 10 steps despite healthy Courant numbers.
root_cause: setFields initialized k and epsilon with free-stream textbook values far too large for the near-wall resolution; the resulting nut over-predicted diffusion, decoupled the solution and drove bounded turbulence quantities negative.
fix: Re-initialize with k/epsilon computed from a conservative turbulence intensity (0.5-1%) and the local velocity scale, or start from a potentialFoam / laminar precursor; consider bounding k and epsilon (bounded schemes or 'bounding' entries) for the first 100 steps.

title: Abrupt refinement transition — residual sawtooth oscillation
symptoms: p residuals oscillated in a stable sawtooth (drop 2 decades, bounce back 1) and never converged; the pattern repeated every ~100 iterations. Mesh had a 4:1 volume jump between refinement levels over a single cell layer; no divergence, just endless oscillation.
root_cause: A single-layer jump between refinement levels creates sudden coefficient changes across the interface; the algebraic multigrid solver ping-pongs between the two cell sizes and locks into a limit cycle.
fix: Smooth the refinement transition (2-3 layers with graded ratios ~1.3-1.5 between levels), or switch the linear solver to smoothSolver/GaussSeidel with cacheAgglomeration for p; verify the oscillation period matches the interface cell count.
